lessons.title: Loops and decisions together
lessons.summary: Putting an if/elif/else check inside a loop that repeats a known number of times.
lessons.worked_example_note: Each of the 5 readings gets its own fresh if/elif/else check — nothing is remembered between passes.

lessons.title: Building up a result step by step
lessons.summary: Tracking more than one running value at once, with decisions guiding what gets counted.
lessons.notes:
Longer problems often need several trackers going through the same loop at once — a running total *and* a count *and* something decided by an if statement. Set every tracker up **before** the loop starts, then update whichever ones apply on each pass.

```python
total = 0
above = 0
for i in range(n):
    score = int(input())
    total = total + score
    if score > 50:
        above = above + 1
```

`total` updates on every pass. `above` only updates when the if condition is true.
lessons.worked_example:
n = int(input())
total = 0
above = 0
for i in range(n):
    score = int(input())
    total = total + score
    if score > 50:
        above = above + 1
print(total)
print(above)
lessons.worked_example_note: Two separate trackers, both set up before the loop — only `above` depends on the if check.

lessons.title: Exam-style combined problems
lessons.summary: Choosing the right loop, tracking what's needed, and branching — all in one program.
lessons.notes:
Combined exam questions ask the same planning question as before, just with more moving parts: **do I know how many times?** — but now you may also need a *validation* while loop first (for a count that must be in range), before the main for loop that reads and classifies each item.

Build longer scenarios in stages: get the count validated first, set up every tracker you'll need, then write the loop body last.
lessons.worked_example_note: The validation while loop and the counting for loop are two separate loops, one after another — not nested inside each other.

quiz.question: Can a loop's body contain a full if/elif/else block?
options: Yes — a loop can repeat any statement, including a whole selection block
No, loops can only contain print statements
Only while loops can contain if statements
Only if the loop repeats exactly once
quiz.answer: Yes — a loop can repeat any statement, including a whole selection block

quiz.question: In a loop that reads and classifies N items, does the if/elif/else check remember anything from the previous pass?
options: No — it runs fresh every single pass, using only that pass's own value
Yes, it remembers the last result
Only the first and last passes are checked
It skips every other pass
quiz.answer: No — it runs fresh every single pass, using only that pass's own value

quiz.question: A program tracks a running total AND a count of values above 50. Where should both variables be created?
options: Both before the loop starts, then updated inside it
Both inside the loop, every pass
Only the total needs setting up first
It doesn't matter
quiz.answer: Both before the loop starts, then updated inside it

quiz.question: In the pattern total = total + score; if score > 50: above = above + 1, does above increase on every pass?
options: No — only on passes where the if condition is true
Yes, on every single pass
No, it never increases
Only on the first pass
quiz.answer: No — only on passes where the if condition is true

quiz.question: A combined exam question needs a validated count AND then a loop that reads that many items. Which comes first?
options: The validation loop for the count, then the counting loop that reads the items
The counting loop, then validation
They must run at exactly the same time
Validation is never needed in combined questions
quiz.answer: The validation loop for the count, then the counting loop that reads the items

quiz.question: True or false: a validation while loop and the main for loop that follows it are nested one inside the other.
options: False — they are two separate loops, one after another
True, the for loop is nested inside the while loop
True, but only in exam questions
False, they must be the same loop
quiz.answer: False — they are two separate loops, one after another

tasks.title: Classify each number
tasks.brief: Input a whole number N. Input N whole numbers, one at a time. For each one, print `Positive` if it's greater than 0, or `Not positive` otherwise.
hints: The if/else inside the loop runs fresh for every number you read.
Loop N times, reading a value and printing its result before moving on to the next one.

tasks.title: Pass or fail each student
tasks.brief: Input a whole number N. Input N whole number test scores, one at a time. For each one, print `Pass` if it's 40 or more, or `Fail` otherwise.
hints: "40 or more" includes exactly 40, so use >= rather than >.
Loop N times, printing the right result for each score before moving to the next one.

tasks.title: Count how many pass
tasks.brief: Input a whole number N. Input N whole number test scores, one at a time. Print how many of them are 40 or more.
hints: Set a counter to 0 before the loop, then increase it whenever a score meets the pass mark.
Loop N times, checking each score with an if statement inside the loop.

tasks.title: Warn about low stock
tasks.brief: Input a whole number N. Input N stock counts, one at a time. For each one, print `Reorder` if it's below 5, or `OK` otherwise.
hints: "Below 5" does not include exactly 5, so use < rather than <=.
Loop N times, printing Reorder or OK for each stock count before moving to the next one.

tasks.title: Grade each score
tasks.brief: Input a whole number N. Input N whole number test scores, one at a time. For each one, print `Distinction` for 90 or above, `Merit` for 70 or above, `Pass` for 40 or above, or `Fail` otherwise.
hints: This combines the elif-chain pattern from Selection with the loop pattern from this lesson — check the highest band first.
Loop N times, running a full elif chain on each score before moving to the next one.

tasks.title: Total and count above 50
tasks.brief: Input a whole number N. Input N whole numbers, one at a time. Print the total of all of them, then on the next line print how many were above 50.
hints: Two trackers, both set up before the loop — the total updates every pass, but the count only updates when the if condition is true.
Update the running total on every pass, and only increase the second counter inside the if statement.

tasks.title: Bonus points
tasks.brief: Input a whole number N. Input N whole number scores, one at a time. Add each score to a running total — but if a score is exactly 100, add one extra bonus point on top of it. Print the final total.
hints: Add the score to the total first, then check separately whether it also earns the bonus point.
The bonus only applies inside the if statement, on top of the addition that already happens every pass.

tasks.title: Passes and fails separately
tasks.brief: Input a whole number N. Input N whole number test scores, one at a time. Print how many scored 40 or more, then on the next line print how many scored below 40.
hints: Two counters, one for each outcome — exactly one of them increases on every pass.
The pattern is `if score >= 40: passed += 1 else: failed += 1`, inside the loop.

tasks.title: Highest of the positives
tasks.brief: Input a whole number N. Input N whole numbers, one at a time — some may be negative. Track the highest value seen so far, but only among the positive ones. Print the highest positive value found. If none of the N numbers are positive, print `None`.
hints: Only update the running highest when the current value is both positive and bigger than what's tracked so far — that's two conditions to check together.
Start the tracker as "nothing yet" so the first positive value found can always become the new highest.

tasks.title: Three trackers
tasks.brief: Input a whole number N. Input N whole number scores, one at a time. Print the total of all of them, then the highest score, then how many of them were exactly 100 (a perfect score) — each on its own line.
hints: Three separate trackers, all set up before the loop, each updated by its own rule inside it.
One tracker updates every pass (the total), one compares against the running highest, and one only increases for an exact match.

tasks.title: Validated attendance register
tasks.brief: Input a whole number for how many students there are — if it isn't between 1 and 30 inclusive, keep asking until it is. Then input that many attendance statuses, one at a time, each either `in` or `out`. Print how many students are marked `in`.
hints: Validate the student count the same way as the Iteration lesson's validation example, then loop that many times reading statuses.
Compare each status exactly to "in" inside the loop, counting the matches.

tasks.title: Multi-part average with grade
tasks.brief: Input a whole number for how many test scores there are — if it isn't between 1 and 30 inclusive, keep asking until it is. Then input that many whole number test scores, one at a time. Print the average, rounded to 1 decimal place, then print `Merit` if the average is 70 or above, or `Pass` otherwise.
hints: Validate the count first, the same way as before, then use the running-total-then-divide pattern for the average.
Compare the rounded average against the boundary to decide which word to print.

tasks.title: Longest streak of passes
tasks.brief:
Input a whole number N. Input N whole number test scores, one at a time. Print the length of the longest run of consecutive passes in a row (a pass is 40 or more). A single fail breaks the streak back to zero.

For example, scores 50, 60, 30, 45, 70, 80 have a streak of 2 (50, 60), which breaks at 30, then a streak of 3 (45, 70, 80) — the longest is 3.
hints: Track two values: the current streak (reset to 0 on a fail) and the longest streak seen so far (only updated when the current one grows past it).
Increase the current streak on a pass and compare it against the longest-so-far; reset the current streak to 0 on any fail.

tasks.title: Delivery cost with validation
tasks.brief: Input a whole number for how many parcels there are — if it isn't between 1 and 20 inclusive, keep asking until it is. Then input that many parcel weights in kg, one at a time (each may include decimals) — if a weight isn't greater than 0, keep asking again for that same parcel. Each parcel costs £2 per kg, and parcels over 10kg get an extra £5 handling fee added to their own cost. Print the total cost of all parcels, rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: Two separate validations are needed: one for the number of parcels, and a second while loop for each individual weight.
Work out each parcel's own cost (with its own handling fee if it applies) before adding it to the running total.

projectTasks.title: Class attendance tracker — Part A: counting present
projectTasks.brief:
A school is building an attendance tracker, split into three parts — each part builds directly on the code you write for the one before it, so keep what you've written rather than starting over.

**Part A.** Read the number of students in a class. Then, for each student, read whether they were `present` or `absent`. Print how many were present, in the format `Present: <n>`.
hints: Use a for loop to read one status per student. Store each status in a list as you go, not just a running count — later parts of this project reuse the full list.
statuses = []; for _ in range(size): s = input(); statuses.append(s) — then print(f"Present: {statuses.count('present')}").

tests.stdin:
6
absent
absent
present
present
present
absent

projectTasks.title: Class attendance tracker — Part B: attendance rating
projectTasks.brief: **Part B.** Your code carries on from Part A — keep everything you already wrote and add to it. No new input needed. After your Part A line, print the number absent, then `Low attendance` if more than 20% of the class was absent, otherwise `Good attendance`.
hints: Don't delete your Part A code — the number absent is the class size minus the number present, both of which you can get from your statuses list.
absent = size - statuses.count('present') — then compare it to 20% of the class size (size * 0.2), printing the new lines after your existing Present line.

tests.stdin:
6
absent
absent
present
present
present
absent

projectTasks.title: Class attendance tracker — Part C: longest streak
projectTasks.brief: **Part C.** Keep everything from Parts A and B. No new input needed — reuse the statuses list you already built. Work out the longest run of consecutive `present` entries in a row, and print it as a final new line, `Longest streak: <n>`.
hints: Loop over your statuses list, keeping a running "current streak" that grows by 1 on each present and resets to 0 on each absent, remembering the biggest it ever reached.

Track two counters as you loop over statuses: one for the current run of presents (reset to 0 on any absent), and one for the longest run seen so far, updated whenever the current run beats it — printed after your existing lines.

Absent: 1
Good attendance
Longest streak: 2

absent
absent
present
present
present
absent

Absent: 3
Low attendance
Longest streak: 3

practiceTasks.title: Count positives
practiceTasks.brief: Input a whole number N, then N more whole numbers, one per line. Print how many of them are positive (greater than 0).
hints: Read each number inside the loop, checking it against 0 as you go.
count = 0, then for i in range(n): value = int(input()); if value > 0: count = count + 1 - then print count.

practiceTasks.title: Shoe size check
practiceTasks.brief: A shop stocks sizes 3 to 12. Input a whole number N, then N requested shoe sizes, one per line. For each one, print `Available` if it's between 3 and 12 inclusive, otherwise print `Out of stock`.
hints: Each size gets checked and printed for straight away, inside the loop.
for i in range(n): size = int(input()); if size >= 3 and size <= 12: print("Available") else: print("Out of stock").

tests.expect:
Available
Out of stock
Out of stock

Out of stock
Available
Available
Out of stock

practiceTasks.title: Highest even number
practiceTasks.brief: Input a whole number N, then N more whole numbers. Print the highest one that is even. If none of them are even, print `None`.
hints: Only update your "highest even so far" tracker when a number is both even and bigger than what you've already got.
Start a variable at None; inside the loop, if the number is even and (the tracker is still None or the number beats it), update the tracker. Print "None" if it's still None afterwards.

practiceTasks.title: Count and total odd numbers
practiceTasks.brief: Input a whole number N, then N more whole numbers. Print how many of them are odd, then print the total of just the odd ones.
hints: Track a count and a total together, both only updating when a number is odd.
count = 0, total = 0, then inside the loop: if value % 2 != 0: count = count + 1; total = total + value.

practiceTasks.title: Bus occupancy
practiceTasks.brief:
A bus starts empty. Input a whole number N, the number of stops. At each stop, input how many people get on, then how many people get off (there are always enough people on the bus to get off).

Print two lines: how many people are on the bus after the final stop, then the highest number of people that were on the bus at any point, counted after each stop.
hints: Keep a running total that changes at every stop, and a separate "highest ever seen" tracker that only ever goes up.
on_board = 0, max_seen = 0; each stop: on_board = on_board + got_on - got_off; if on_board > max_seen: max_seen = on_board.

practiceTasks.title: Count the passes
practiceTasks.brief:
Input a whole number N (at least 1), then N test marks (whole numbers, one per line). A mark of 50 or more is a pass. Print `Passes: ` followed by how many of the marks were passes.

For example, `3` followed by `70`, `40`, `50` prints `Passes: 2`.
hints: You need a loop to read the marks and a selection inside it to test each one.
Keep a counter, `passes = 0`, and add 1 when `mark >= 50`.

practiceTasks.title: Fizz and buzz
practiceTasks.brief:
Input a whole number N (at least 1). For every number from 1 to N, print a line:
- `FizzBuzz` if the number is divisible by both 3 and 5
- `Fizz` if it is divisible by 3 (but not 5)
- `Buzz` if it is divisible by 5 (but not 3)
- otherwise, the number itself

For example, `5` prints `1`, `2`, `Fizz`, `4`, `Buzz` on five lines.
hints: Loop from 1 to N. Inside the loop, check the 'both' case FIRST, otherwise it would be caught by one of the others.
A number is divisible by 3 when `i % 3 == 0`. Use `if` / `elif` / `elif` / `else`.

practiceTasks.title: Pass, merit or fail count
practiceTasks.brief:
Input a whole number N (at least 1), then N marks out of 100 (one per line). Each mark is a `Merit` if 70 or more, a `Pass` if 40 to 69, and a `Fail` if below 40.

Print three lines: `Merit: <count>`, `Pass: <count>` and `Fail: <count>`.
hints: Use three separate counters, all starting at 0.
Inside the loop use `if / elif / else` to decide which counter to add 1 to.

practiceTasks.title: Stop on the word stop
practiceTasks.brief: Input words, one per line, until the word `stop` is entered. The word `stop` itself is not counted. Print `Words: ` followed by how many words were entered before `stop`, and then `Longest: ` followed by the longest of those words (if two are tied, the first). If `stop` is the first word, print `Words: 0` and `Longest: none`.
hints: You do not know how many words there will be, so use a `while` loop that reads a word each time round.
Keep a counter and a variable for the longest word so far. Replace the longest only when the new word is strictly longer.

practiceTasks.title: Times table check
practiceTasks.brief:
Input a times table number from 1 to 12. Then input three answers, one per line: the answers a student gave to table × 1, table × 2 and table × 3, in that order.

For each answer print `Correct` if it is right or `Wrong` if it is not. Finish by printing `Score: ` followed by how many were correct, then `/3`.

For example, the table `5` with the answers `5`, `11` and `15` prints `Correct`, `Wrong`, `Correct` and `Score: 2/3`.
hints: Read the table number first, then use a `for` loop with `i` from 1 to 3. The correct answer for question `i` is `table * i`.
Compare each answer with `table * i`, print `Correct` or `Wrong`, and keep a score counter that goes up when it is correct.

practiceTasks.title: Vowels and consonants
practiceTasks.brief:
Input a word in lower case (letters only). Print two lines: `Vowels: ` followed by how many of its letters are a, e, i, o or u, and `Consonants: ` followed by how many of its letters are not.

For example, `python` prints `Vowels: 1` and `Consonants: 5`.
hints: Loop through the letters of the word. Each letter is either a vowel or a consonant.
Two counters. `if letter in "aeiou":` add to the vowel counter, `else:` add to the consonant counter.

practiceTasks.title: Bank balance
practiceTasks.brief:
A bank account starts with a balance of £100. Input a whole number N (at least 1). Then input N transactions, one per line. Each is a whole number: a positive number is money paid in and a negative number is money taken out.

A withdrawal is only allowed if it would not take the balance below £0. If it would, print `Refused` for it and leave the balance unchanged. Otherwise apply it. When all transactions are done, print `Balance: £` followed by the balance.

For example, `2` transactions of `-30` and `-90` prints `Refused` and then `Balance: £70`.
hints: Start with `balance = 100` and loop through the transactions. Add each one to the balance, but check first.
Work out `new_balance = balance + amount`. If `new_balance < 0`, print `Refused`; otherwise set `balance = new_balance`.

practiceTasks.title: Positive, negative and zero
practiceTasks.brief: Input whole numbers, one per line, until the number 999 is entered (the 999 is not counted). Print three lines: `Positive: <count>`, `Negative: <count>` and `Zero: <count>`, counting how many of the numbers were above 0, below 0, and equal to 0.
hints: Use a `while` loop that keeps reading numbers until it gets 999. Use three counters.
Read a number before the loop, then `while number != 999:` test it with `if / elif / else`, update a counter, and read the next number at the bottom of the loop.

practiceTasks.title: 🌟 Guessing game
practiceTasks.brief:
The secret number is 42. Input guesses (whole numbers), one per line, until the guess is correct. For each wrong guess print `Too low` if it is below 42 or `Too high` if it is above 42. When the guess is correct print `Correct in <n> guesses`, where `<n>` is how many guesses were made in total. Always write the word `guesses` like this, even for 1.

For example, the guesses `10`, `50`, `42` print `Too low`, `Too high` and `Correct in 3 guesses`.
hints: Use a `while` loop with a counter for the number of guesses. Read a guess, add 1 to the counter, then test it.
Inside the loop: if the guess is 42, print the result. Otherwise use another `if` to choose between `Too low` and `Too high`. Stop the loop after a correct guess.

practiceTasks.title: 🌟 Word statistics
practiceTasks.brief:
Input a whole number N (at least 1), then N words (one per line). Print three lines:
- `Longest: ` followed by the longest word (if two are tied, the first)
- `Shortest: ` followed by the shortest word (if two are tied, the first)
- `Average length: ` followed by the mean length of the words, rounded to 1 decimal place

For example, `cat`, `elephant`, `dog` prints `Longest: elephant`, `Shortest: cat` and `Average length: 4.7`.
hints: Read the words into a list first. Then you can go through it as many times as you need.
Start with `longest = words[0]` and `shortest = words[0]`, then compare `len(word)` for every other word using `>` and `<`. For the mean, add up all the lengths and divide by N.
